svg.text: The fix I was sure would work
A code knowledge graph, A/B-tested against baseline on the 8 write-flow
requirements it was built to help. What it actually did:
FALSE-POSITIVE RATE — THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS
Baseline (regex hints)
false positives
With the code knowledge graph
no improvement — if anything, worse
COVERAGE, SAME REQUIREMENTS
8 of 8 → 7 of 8
the graph cost one requirement
THE VERDICT
NO-GO. More code knowledge didn't move the metric.
Why it couldn't work — from first principles
A test checks the app's actual behaviour against its EXPECTED behaviour — the oracle.
The oracle is a statement of intent. Intent is not in the code.
Deriving "what it should do" from the code under test is circular — it catches nothing.
No amount of code knowledge can supply a missing oracle.
The lever was never code knowledge — it's the fidelity of the requirement itself.
Differential A/B on the 8 write-flow requirements graph-L1 augmented, 3 runs per arm — a strong directional signal, not a
significance test. The 31.5% is on this harder subset, not the 18.2% full-breadth rate. Source: graphify-decision-memo.md §12 · Cypress RWA
